title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-25
korean_summary: 오늘 핵심: 본사 근로계약 질의에 인사팀 확인 후 회신, 운송사 계약 부록 검토와 화물 보험 대응 결정, 본사 무허가 구역 목록 확인.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Wednesday, November twenty-fifth. Yesterday was Vietnam Culture Day, so the office was closed. Today the week really starts again. Some emails came in during the holiday, so let's catch up on them together.

Here is the plan for the next twenty minutes. There are eight parts. Part one is this opening. Part two is the top three tasks for today. Part three is the reports you need to collect. Part four is the replies you owe. Part five is your schedule and deadlines. Part six is English review. Part seven is a short role-play. Part eight is the closing.

First, some good news from Monday. You confirmed the renewal of the factory insurance with the broker. You sent the Tet holiday flight plan to a new manager and my director. You told the purchasing staff to prepare the purchase request for a former manager's flight. You approved this week's production consumables at a lower total. And you sent the weekly firewood report to head office. That was a busy day before the holiday. Well done.
Let's begin.
Part two. Top three for today.
Number one. Head office's three questions on a worker's contract.

What is it? On Monday evening, a head office manager wrote to you. It is about a worker whose contract ends soon. Last Saturday, you recommended changing her contract to an indefinite one. An indefinite contract has no end date. Before reporting to the CEO, the head office manager wants three more checks.

First, can we talk with the worker? The idea is to pay her the lost benefits in one amount, and end the contract when it expires. Second, if both sides agree, is there still a legal risk? Could there be a dispute or a fine later? Third, if the talk fails, is an indefinite contract the only option?

Why does it matter? This is a sensitive labor case. The law protects workers in this situation strongly. A wrong step could bring a complaint to the labor department. Head office will decide based on your answer.

Your first action today: talk with the HR staff this morning. Ask them about the legal basis for each of the three questions. Then write a short reply with a clear recommendation. Show it to my director before you send it.
Number two. The trucking contracts and cargo insurance.

What is it? This is with the import and export manager. On Monday, she answered your three points. First, the main trucking company will send the revised appendix draft today, by email. Second, and this is important, none of the trucking companies has cargo liability insurance. That insurance pays if our goods are lost or damaged on their truck. The certificates they sent only cover damage to other people. One company's certificate also expired on November fourteenth. Third, she attached the invoice for the highest value shipment on one truck.

Why does it matter? Our new clause says the trucking company buys cargo insurance and pays the full cargo value. But if they have no insurance, they may not be able to pay. One truck can carry a very large amount of our goods. So the clause alone does not protect us.

Your first action today: check the appendix draft as soon as it arrives. Compare it with the standard clauses, article by article. Then decide one point. Will we ask each company to buy cargo insurance by a set date? Or will we keep our own insurance for now? Remember, the other companies must reply by tomorrow, November twenty-sixth.
Number three. The unpermitted area check from head office.

What is it? Yesterday morning, a head office compliance manager sent a file. It lists areas in each factory that do not have a building permit. The email went to my director, and you are copied. Head office asks two things. Is the list different from what we know? And could the way we use these areas create any risk in the future?
Why does it matter? An area without a permit can bring a fine during an inspection. It can also be a fire safety problem. my director will probably ask you to check our part of the list.

Your first action today: open the file and find the rows for our factory. Compare them with our lease contract and the factory layout. Then prepare a short note for my director. For each area, write what it is used for, and the possible risk.
Part three. Reports to collect.

First, from the chief accountant. On Monday, you told her clearly not to change an approved CM again. CM means cutting and making, our sewing fee. You also gave her the decision on some styles that were already exported. Today, check that she applied your decision in the file. You can say: "Please send me the updated file, so that I can check those styles."

Second, from the purchasing staff. a former manager should get his passport back from the police around today. He must leave the country by November twenty-ninth. Please check that the flight purchase request is ready. Check also that the flight date fits his passport date. You can say: "Could you let me know where the purchase request stands? The flight is this Sunday."

Third, from the import and export manager again, on a second topic. Head office logistics asked her yesterday to fill in the blank cells in the January to June shipping report. You can say: "Please fill in the yellow cells and send the file back by Friday."

Fourth, from the broker. You confirmed the renewal on Monday. Now you are waiting for the policy and the debit note. A debit note is the bill. The new period starts on December sixteenth. You can say: "Could you send us the policy and the debit note by early December?"

Fifth, from the compliance officer. Her final quote for the firefighting system maintenance is due tomorrow. Also, the electrical inspection purchase request is due this week. You can say: "Please send me both by Thursday, so that we can finish approval before the quote expires."
Part four. Replies I owe.

Reply one. the head office manager, about the worker's contract. We covered this in part two. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for your questions. Here are our answers after checking with HR."

Reply two. A head office logistics manager. Yesterday, he sent a new rule for air storage charges. Air storage charges are fees for keeping cargo at the airport too long. From now on, we must check the cause, and decide who pays. Then we charge last month's costs by the fifteenth of every month. No reply is needed. But you should give a short instruction to the import and export manager and the accounting team. Your first sentence could be: "From December, please report last month's air storage charges to me by the tenth of each month."

Reply three. the import and export manager, about the trucking insurance. After you decide, tell her clearly. Your first sentence could be: "Since none of the companies has cargo liability insurance, please ask each of them for a plan by December fifth."

Reply four. A head office planning manager. On Monday night, he sent my director two options for the staff welfare plan. my director may ask your opinion. Your first sentence to my director could be: "I checked both options. Option one costs less, but option two is easier to explain to workers."
Part five. Schedule and deadlines.
Today, Wednesday. Check the trucking appendix draft from the main trucking company.

Tomorrow, Thursday, November twenty-sixth. The other trucking companies must reply. The compliance officer's firefighting maintenance quote is due. Your calendar also shows next week's overtime report.
Friday, November twenty-seventh. The weekly cash flow report and the weekly subcontractor report.
Saturday, November twenty-eighth. The monthly stock status update. The curtain for the firewood storage area should also be installed by then.
And next Monday is November thirtieth, the last day of the month. A monthly HR report goes to head office that day.
Part six. English review.
Let's review ten expressions. Four are from today's card, and six are from last week.

The expression is "unauthorized." It means done without approval. For example, "The price change on the invoice was unauthorized, so please revise it." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. The price change on the invoice was unauthorized, so please revise it.

The expression is "specify." It means to write something clearly in a document. For example, "Please ask the supplier to specify the cushion strip in the quotation." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please ask the supplier to specify the cushion strip in the quotation.

The expression is "cap." It means to set a top limit. For example, "Please cap this week's consumables order at our weekly budget." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please cap this week's consumables order at our weekly budget.

The expression is "carry over." It means to move something to the next period or list. For example, "Please carry over the three items to next week's list." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please carry over the three items to next week's list.

The expression is "Please do not do something without my prior approval." It means: ask me first. For example, "Please do not change an approved price without my prior approval." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please do not change an approved price without my prior approval.

The expression is "liable." It means legally responsible to pay for damage. For example, "The trucking company is liable for any damage to the cargo during transport." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. The trucking company is liable for any damage to the cargo during transport.

The expression is "I have yet to receive something, which I asked for on a date." It means I asked, but it has not come. For example, "I have yet to receive the trucking quotation sheets, which I asked for on November nineteenth." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. I have yet to receive the trucking quotation sheets, which I asked for on November nineteenth.

The expression is "rationale." It means the reason behind a decision. For example, "Please explain the rationale for the CM change for each style." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please explain the rationale for the CM change for each style.

The expression is "I'm not in a position to do something until something happens." It means I cannot do it yet. For example, "I'm not in a position to approve the plan until you explain each style." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. I'm not in a position to approve the plan until you explain each style.

The expression is "My understanding is that something. Please correct me if I'm wrong." It is a polite way to check a fact. For example, "My understanding is that our team books the trucks directly. Please correct me if I'm wrong." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. My understanding is that our team books the trucks directly. Please correct me if I'm wrong.

And one bonus expression for today's trucking work. The expression is "cross-check." It means to compare one document with another to make sure they match. For example, "Who cross-checks the trucking invoice against the booking?" Today, you can use it like this: "I will cross-check the appendix against our standard clauses." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. I will cross-check the appendix against our standard clauses.
Part seven. Role-play.
Today's situation. You talk with the import and export manager about the trucking contracts and cargo insurance. Listen first.
Anthony: Good morning. Did the appendix draft from the main trucking company arrive?
Manager: Yes, Anthony. It came this morning. I will forward it to you now.
Anthony: Thank you. Does it include all the articles, without changes?
Manager: I think so. But please check two of the articles.
Anthony: I will. Now, about insurance. My understanding is that none of the companies has cargo liability insurance. Please correct me if I'm wrong.
Manager: That's right. They only have the compulsory vehicle insurance.
Anthony: Then the new clause is not enough. If a truck has an accident, they may not be able to pay.
Manager: Should I ask them to buy cargo insurance?
Anthony: Yes. Please ask each company for a plan. When can they buy it, and what is the sum insured?
Manager: What if they say it is too expensive?
Anthony: Then ask for the price, and tell me. We will decide whether to keep our own insurance for now.
Manager: OK. And one company's certificate expired. I already asked them for the new one.
Anthony: Good. Please send me everything by December fifth.
Manager: Noted, Anthony.
Now, let's practice two key sentences.

Sentence one. "Since none of the companies has cargo liability insurance, please ask each of them for a plan." Say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Since none of the companies has cargo liability insurance, please ask each of them for a plan.

Sentence two. "We will decide whether to keep our own insurance for now." Say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. We will decide whether to keep our own insurance for now.
Part eight. Closing.

Today has three main tasks. First, answer head office's three questions on the worker's contract, after checking with HR and my director. Second, check the trucking appendix and decide on cargo insurance. Third, check our rows in the unpermitted area list for my director.
If you remember only one thing, remember this. Talk with HR this morning, and send head office a clear answer on the worker's contract today.
You are ready. Have a good day, Anthony.
